Simple-ZipNeRF is a regularized variant of ZipNeRF designed to mitigate floater artifacts in sparse input scenarios by introducing an auxiliary "augmented" model with reduced capacity [S1].

The claim states that Simple-ZipNeRF is a regularized variant of ZipNeRF designed to mitigate floater artifacts in sparse input scenarios by introducing an auxiliary 'augmented' model with reduced capacity. The evidence supports this: [S1] notes explicitly mention that Simple-ZipNeRF is part of the 'Simple Radiance Fields' family which regularizes models to choose simpler solutions. It states that for ZipNeRF, the augmented model is designed by reducing the size of the hash table (reduced from $2^{21}$ to $2^{11}$, which is a reduction in capacity) to prevent floater artifacts caused by the large hash table in sparse settings. The notes also confirm that the augmented model is used to generate depth priors for regularizing the main ZipNeRF.
